thread.title: Judge denies Minnesota effort to extradite ICE agent from Texas - NewsBreak
thread.title_full: Judge denies Minnesota effort to extradite ICE agent from Texas - NewsBreak

author: Emilio Perez Ibarguen
title: Judge denies Minnesota effort to extradite ICE agent from Texas - NewsBreak
text:
By Emilio Perez Ibarguen ,
3 hours ago
A federal judge Wednesday evening denied Minnesota’s bid to force Texas Gov. Greg Abbott to extradite an Immigration and Customs Enforcement agent charged in connection with a January nonfatal shooting during enforcement activity.
In a 13-page ruling , District Judge Fernando Rodriguez Jr., wrote that the court “is unaware of any authority supporting the creation of a court-imposed deadline” for extraditing individuals to the states where they’ve been charged.
Minnesota officials charged the ICE officer, Christian Castro, in May with four counts of second-degree assault and one count of falsely reporting a crime after he shot Julio Sosa-Celis, a Venezuelan national, in the leg through the door of a Minneapolis home. Castro was arrested in Texas that month in connection with those charges, after Minnesota issued a nationwide warrant for his arrest, and remains in custody in Brownsville, Texas.
But earlier this month, Minnesota Attorney General Keith Ellison sued Abbott to force Castro’s extradition, arguing that Abbott was violating his responsibility to issue a rendition warrant for Castro under interstate extradition laws amid a Texas review of whether Castro qualifies as a fugitive. Ellison, in an August filing , also expressed concern that Castro could flee the country if let go from jail.
Texas law dictates that Castro must be released after 90 days, which is Thursday, unless extradited elsewhere.
Rodriguez, however, ruled that, although Abbott “has considered this particular extradition request for an atypically long duration,” Minnesota had not demonstrated any actual requirement for Texas to extradite Castro within a specific time period.
Abbott's press secretary, Andrew Mahaleris, said in a statement Wednesday that the order protects Texas’ constitutional duty to carefully consider extradition requests and “rebuffs Minnesota’s efforts to conscript federal courts into commandeering the authority of Governor Abbott’s office.”
But Minnesota Gov. Tim Walz argued the request fell within the norms of the states' relationship, saying in a statement that “Texas has previously fulfilled every extradition — as has Minnesota — and this case should be no different.”
Ellison, in a statement, said the state would “continue litigating this case" but didn’t specify exactly how it would do so, adding that Abbot is “turning Texas into a sanctuary state for violent criminals.”
Ellison had previously told reporters that the state had made repeated attempts to compel Abbott to greenlight the extradition but that they were repeatedly ignored.
